eyebrow: Day one of a blank subscription

steps.label: No identity baseline
steps.sub: a local admin login, not the company's real identity provider

steps.label: No network path
steps.sub: isolated from shared services, logging, and everything else

steps.label: No active policy
steps.sub: nothing stops a public storage bucket or an untagged resource

eyebrow: What a landing zone provides before day one

steps.label: Identity & access
steps.sub: wired to the real identity provider, not a shared admin password

steps.label: Network connectivity
steps.sub: already peered to shared services, DNS, and egress controls

steps.label: Policy guardrails
steps.sub: actively enforced, not a wiki page asking teams to remember

steps.label: Logging & cost tracking
steps.sub: centralized and tagged from the very first resource created

code:
# cost of adding governance is roughly proportional to
# how much already exists WITHOUT it
#
# retrofit tagging onto 200 existing resources  -> expensive project
# retrofit segmentation after dev reaches prod   -> incident response
# build identity + network + policy before day 1 -> near-zero marginal cost
caption: The landing zone pattern exists because the cheapest point to govern a workload is before it's created.
